The best free OCR tools for images and scans, compared

OCR turns a photo, screenshot or scanned PDF into text you can copy and edit. The free options differ a lot in languages, limits and where your scan goes. Here is what each says about itself.

We make Slop OCR, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • Languages it can read
  • Free limits: files, pages and size
  • Outputs: text, Word, searchable PDF
  • Where the scan is processed: your device or their servers
  • Whether you need an account or an install

1. Slop OCR (ours)

Best for: Private scans in English or Simplified Chinese, many pages at once

Reads text from photos, screenshots and every page of a scanned PDF in the browser, shows a box around each line, and lets you fix the text before saving.

Good

  • Nothing is uploaded: the scan is read on your device
  • Every page of a PDF, read at 200 dpi
  • Edit the text before you save it
  • Save as text, Markdown, Word or a searchable PDF, or copy

Not so good

  • Two languages only: English and Simplified Chinese
  • Needs a one-time model download (about 15 MB) before the first read
  • Slower on old phones and computers than a server

Open Slop OCR

2. Google Drive

Best for: People who already use Google Drive and Docs

Good

  • Open an image or PDF with Google Docs and the text appears in a document
  • Detects the language itself, with a long list of languages
  • Keeps bold, italics, font size and line breaks in many cases

Not so good

  • Files should be 2 MB or smaller
  • Lists, tables, columns and footnotes are not likely to be detected
  • The file is uploaded to your Google Drive

Google Drive website · Sources: Convert images to text (Google Drive Help)

3. OnlineOCR.net

Best for: Getting Word or Excel files out of a few scans

Good

  • 46 recognition languages
  • Outputs Word, Excel, PDF, RTF and plain text
  • No registration for guest use

Not so good

  • Guests can convert 5 files an hour
  • Files are uploaded to the service
  • Registered users' output files are stored for a month

OnlineOCR.net website · Sources: OnlineOCR.net

4. i2OCR

Best for: Rare languages, one page at a time

Good

  • 128 languages
  • Download as text, Word, HTML or searchable PDF
  • Single or multi-column layout setting

Not so good

  • Free OCR handles one image or page at a time
  • Bulk OCR needs a premium plan
  • Files are uploaded for processing

i2OCR website · Sources: i2OCR

5. Tesseract

Best for: Developers and batch jobs on your own computer, in 100+ languages

Good

  • Recognises more than 100 languages out of the box
  • Outputs plain text, hOCR, PDF, invisible-text PDF, TSV, ALTO and PAGE
  • Runs on your own computer; can be trained for other languages

Not so good

  • No graphical app: it is a command-line program and library
  • Opens images, not PDF documents
  • Better results often need you to clean up the image first

Tesseract website · Sources: Tesseract README

Which one to choose

For private documents in English or Simplified Chinese, Slop OCR fits our criteria best: no account, no cap, many pages at once, and the scan never leaves your device. For any other language it is the wrong tool.

For other languages, i2OCR (128) and OnlineOCR.net (46) work in the browser but upload your file and limit free use. Google Drive is handy if you live in Google Docs, within 2 MB per file. Tesseract is the choice for developers and large batches on your own machine, if you are happy with the command line.

Questions

What is the best free OCR that does not upload my scan?

Slop OCR reads the text in your browser, so the image or PDF stays on your device. Tesseract also runs on your computer, as a command-line program. Google Drive, OnlineOCR.net and i2OCR process the file on their servers.

Which free OCR reads the most languages?

i2OCR lists 128 languages and Tesseract more than 100. OnlineOCR.net lists 46. Slop OCR reads English and Simplified Chinese.

Can I get a searchable PDF for free?

Yes. Slop OCR, i2OCR and Tesseract can save a PDF with an invisible text layer, so you can search and copy the words.

Can OCR read a whole scanned PDF?

Slop OCR reads every page of a PDF in one go. Google Drive opens multipage PDFs, while i2OCR's free plan does one page at a time and OnlineOCR.net allows 5 files an hour for guests.
